stories.author: Judd Legum
stories.title: UPDATE: Katie Zacharia’s disastrous response to Popular Information’s report
stories.text: Zacharia has repeatedly said she was “outside counsel” to the World Bank and “general counsel” to a California non-profit. Trump himself touted Zacharia as an “attorney” in his post announcing her appointment on Truth Social. On Tuesday morning, Popular Information reported that there was no evidence that Zacharia was ever licensed to practice law in any state. A few hours later, Trump was confronted with Popular Information’s report on the South Lawn of the White House by the New York Times’ Shawn McCreesh. Trump motioned to Zacharia, who was standing behind him, to answer the question: Q: You said she’s an attorney. Where did she pass the bar exam? Which state? TRUMP (to Zacharia): Which state? ZACHARIA: When I moved to China. Q: Where did you pass the bar exam? Watch: When Zacharia was pressed again, she appeared to wave the question away. Zacharia’s answer makes no sense. China’s bar exam is not available to U.S. citizens and U.S. states do not offer bar exams in China. On Tuesday afternoon, Zacharia provided a somewhat different response to Politico’s Dasha Burns. “ I practiced international transactional law, with all the appropriate credentials ,” Zacharia said. stories.title: Mike Rogers’s Wife Raked in Lucrative Government Security Contracts While Rogers Served as Intel Chair
stories.text: Mike Rogers and his second wife, Kristi, saw their wealth rise substantially after Rogers was elevated to chair of the House Intelligence Committee in 2011 and lucrative government contracts poured her way, a review of financial disclosures finds. Rogers was first elected to Congress in 2000, in time to be a major backer of the Iraq war. With a background at the FBI, Rogers was encouraged by Speaker Dennis Hastert to get involved in foreign policy and national security matters. According to the Rogers Archive at Oakland University, he made seven trips to Iraq between 2001 and 2005 as a member of Congress. In 2005, he was appointed to the House Intelligence Committee. (Drop Site could not independently verify the number of trips, but taking seven trips to Iraq in the space of four years would be highly unusual for a member of Congress—and trips in 2001 or 2002, before the invasion, are unlikely.) Kristi Clemens was a top press aide to L. Paul Bremer, who oversaw the U.S. occupation of Iraq as head of the Coalition Provisional Authority. stories.title: Democrats for Mike Rogers Coalition Is Powered by Right-Wingers
stories.text: Story by Tom Perkins In August, Michigan’s Republican nominee for U.S. Senate, Mike Rogers, stood at a podium in a Detroit front yard with a small group of political and religious leaders who identified themselves as Democrats. Abdul El-Sayed, Rogers’s Democratic opponent, was too extreme, they said, compelling them to take the unprecedented step of supporting a Republican. Rogers called them “courageous.” “I’m not asking you to be a Republican. I’m asking you for the opportunity to earn your trust,” Rogers reportedly said. “Michigan deserves a senator who will sit down, whether you voted for me or not, and will listen to you. Will treat you with respect. Will represent everybody.” They are part of a group called Democrats for Mike Rogers, and among their leaders is Michigan State Rep. Karen Whitsett, the treasurer of the Democrats for Mike Rogers super PAC, which has spent about $4.4 million in support of Rogers or against El-Sayed, according to federal filings , and helped fuel the narrative that Democrats are backing Rogers in meaningful numbers. stories.author: Ken Klippenstein
stories.title: Exclusive: How the Military Will Hack the Election
stories.text: U.S. CYBERCOM troops I’m alarmed how little attention is being paid to the military’s unprecedented involvement in our election. I really want to stay on this story and find out what CYBERCOM is doing. This military task force is secretly at work as part of a government-wide “election security group,” guarding against “interference” in the upcoming midterm elections. Interference, however, is a loaded word. While it connotes the Kremlin hacking into polling places or changing the election count, Task Force Raider is actually more focused on the broader category of “influence”, specifically Russian or Chinese attempts to change minds rather than to change votes. But the real target is the American people, whom the federal government sees as vectors for foreign influence. “The entire election security scare is to indulge President Trump and assuage Democrats, all of whom fear interference and shenanigans, but not from foreign shores,” says a senior military intelligence officer, who spoke to me about the secret effort. stories.title: Destruction of Gaza Court System Strips Women of Their Rights
stories.text: GAZA CITY—Standing before the rubble of the Palace of Justice in central Gaza, Salma Abdel Hadi was overwhelmed by a profound sense of helplessness. Since her husband’s killing last year, the 38-year-old mother of six has been unable to secure inheritance rights for herself and her children to help provide food and clothing in the midst of a genocide. The Israeli military deliberately destroyed the Palace of Justice in Al-Zahra City early in the war, rigging the court complex with explosives and demolishing the entire structure on December 4, 2023. Abdel Hadi’s husband was killed in an Israeli airstrike in August 2025, leaving her alone to raise and feed their children in the Nuseirat refugee camp—and with no functioning court system, accessing any of her late husband’s money or property has been all but impossible. “My children need their rights more than ever,” Abdel Hadi told Drop Site News, clasping her hands together in anguish. “But today I find myself facing a question to which I have no answer: How can I protect my children’s right to inherit from their father if the place that is supposed to provide me with a document proving that right has been reduced to rubble?” In the
